english.title: Supply of an unauthorised veterinary medicinal product
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) supplied an unauthorised veterinary medicinal product, namely **(..SPECIFY PRODUCT..), to **(..SPECIFY RECIPIENT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 27(1), 43(s) and 44(1) of the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013.
english.pointstoprove:
date and Location
supply unauthorised veterinary medicinal product

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This regulation does not apply to;
(a) a veterinary medicinal product prescribed by a veterinary surgeon under the cascade; or
(b) a product supplied in accordance with a certificate granted by the Secretary of State under these regulations - section 27(2)

(ii) It is a defence for a person charged with failing to comply with section 27(1) to prove that the supply was for the purpose of research or development of a veterinary medicinal product - section 25(3)

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
